title: An Unexpected Robot Policy: Early Evaluations of GPT-6 Astra on RoboDojo and Beyond
abstract: Embodied AI systems are often organized into System 1 and System 2. System 1 is typically a pretrained policy that generates actions at high frequency, whereas System 2 is often instantiated as a vision-enabled language model for high-level planning. We ask whether a large language model (LLM) can act as the policy for robot manipulation without task-specific finetuning. We call this setting LLM as policy. We evaluate three LLMs on all 42 RoboDojo tasks and compare their scores with 40 public policies. Astra and GPT-5.5 use the official 50-episode-per-task protocol; DeepSeek-Flash uses 10 episodes per task. GPT-6 Astra achieves 22.48% average success rate and 28.97 Score over 2,100 trials, ranking above every public entry. Yet GPT-5.5 and DeepSeek-Flash reach only 0.88% and 1.92% average success rate with the same post-processing. We find that Astra exhibits a sharply polarized capability profile. It generalizes well to tasks that require semantic understanding but not high-precision control. In contrast, it performs poorly on tasks that require precision, dynamic control, or complex bimanual coordination. In-context experiments show no aggregate benefit from one-shot demonstrations, while selected interaction traces show within-episode corrections under perturbations. Overall, the evaluated LLMs vary substantially in manipulation performance. Astra stands out and provides initial evidence for the potential of a general-purpose manipulation model, although reliable precision and dynamic control remain limitations in the evaluated setting.

segments.speaker: John
segments.en: Welcome to Advanced Topics in Embodied AI. Today's lecture is on a recent paper investigating GPT-6 Astra as a direct robotic policy. The field has seen a significant push towards dual-system architectures, where one model handles slow reasoning and another handles fast motor control, like in the 'Fast-in-Slow' framework or the paradigm described in 'Robobench'. This paper challenges that division by asking if a single, large model can do both jobs at once. Yes, Noah?
segments.zh: 欢迎来到具身智能进阶专题。今天这堂课讲一篇最近的论文，研究的是把GPT-6 Astra直接当作机器人策略来用。这个领域最近有一股很强的趋势，就是搞双系统架构，一个模型负责慢速推理，另一个负责快速运动控制，比如Fast-in-Slow框架或者Robobench里描述的那种范式。这篇论文对这种分工提出了挑战，它问的是：一个单一的大模型能不能同时把这两件事都干了。好，Noah？

segments.speaker: Noah
segments.en: Hi Professor. So is the central claim here that we don't need separate motor policies like VLAs or WAMs anymore?
segments.zh: 教授您好。所以这里的核心主张是，我们不再需要像VLA或WAM那样单独的动作策略了吗？

segments.speaker: John
segments.en: That's the core question it investigates. It argues that for certain tasks, a frozen language model can select executable manipulation targets directly, but the conclusion is much more nuanced than a simple replacement. The research shows Astra is an unexpectedly capable but sharply uneven policy.
segments.zh: 这正是它要研究的核心问题。论文主张，在某些任务上，一个冻结的语言模型可以直接选出可执行的操作目标，但结论远比简单替换要微妙得多。研究表明，Astra 是一个能力出乎意料地强、但表现又极不均衡的策略。

segments.speaker: John
segments.en: The conventional wisdom, as we've discussed, is to split the problem. A large language model performs high-level, semantic planning—what you might call System 2 thinking. It decides to 'pick up the red block'. Then, it hands that subgoal to a pretrained Vision-Language-Action, or VLA, model. That's the System 1, the fast motor controller that executes the physical action. This paper proposes collapsing that hierarchy. The core idea is to have one model handle both roles.
segments.zh: 我们之前讨论过，传统思路是把问题拆开。大语言模型负责高层的语义规划，也就是所谓的系统2思维。它决定“拿起红色方块”。然后把这个子目标交给预训练的视觉-语言-动作模型，也就是VLA模型。这就是系统1，快速的动作控制器，负责执行物理动作。这篇论文提出把这个层级结构压平。核心思路是让一个模型同时承担这两个角色。

segments.speaker: Noah
segments.en: So the LLM is generating robot joint commands directly?
segments.zh: 所以大语言模型是直接生成机器人的关节指令吗？

segments.speaker: John
segments.en: Not quite. And this is a key distinction they make. The model interprets the scene from camera views and outputs world-frame end-effector targets—basically, 'move this hand to this specific coordinate with this orientation'. That target is then passed to non-learned, geometric post-processing software that handles inverse kinematics and motion planning to generate the joint commands. They define 'LLM as policy' as a frozen LLM with no learned policy between it and the robot, and no task-specific fine-tuning. The geometric conversion is allowed because it isn't a learned skill.
segments.zh: 不完全是。这是他们强调的一个关键区别。模型从摄像头视角理解场景，输出世界坐标系下的末端执行器目标——基本上就是“把这只手以这个姿态移动到这个具体坐标”。然后这个目标会传给非学习的几何后处理软件，由它来处理逆运动学和运动规划，生成关节指令。他们把“LLM作为策略”定义为：一个冻结的LLM，在它和机器人之间没有任何学习到的策略，也没有针对特定任务的微调。几何转换是允许的，因为它不是一种学习到的技能。

segments.speaker: Noah
segments.en: Okay, that makes sense. So how did it perform against the standard two-system approach?
segments.zh: 好，这就说得通了。那它跟标准的双系统方案比起来表现怎么样？

segments.speaker: John
segments.en: Strikingly well, on the surface. On the 42 tasks in the RoboDojo-Sim benchmark, Astra achieved a 22.48% average success rate, ranking it above all 40 public policy entries. But—and this is critical—the capability is highly model-specific. When the same setup was tested with GPT-5.5, it only reached 0.88% success. DeepSeek-Flash hit 1.92%. This isn't a general feature of LLMs; it's an emergent property of a specific, very large model.
segments.zh: 表面上看，表现惊人。在RoboDojo-Sim基准的42项任务上，Astra取得了22.48%的平均成功率，排名高于所有40个公开策略条目。但——这一点至关重要——这种能力高度依赖于特定模型。当同样的设置用GPT-5.5测试时，成功率只有0.88%。DeepSeek-Flash达到1.92%。这不是大语言模型的通用特性，而是某个特定超大模型涌现出的能力。

segments.speaker: John
segments.en: Let's dig into the mechanics of that policy. In each turn of the control loop, the model receives three RGB camera views, robot state information like joint angles, the remaining time, and the instruction. It must then call one of two functions: 'give_up' or 'move_eef'. The 'move_eef' function takes absolute position, orientation, and gripper targets for either or both arms. A non-learned motion planner then attempts to execute this, handling collision checking and joint path planning. If the target is unreachable or invalid, the model gets an error message and can try again. The simulation environment, RoboDojo, is the sole judge of success.
segments.zh: 我们来深入看看这个策略的具体机制。在控制循环的每一轮里，模型会收到三路RGB摄像头画面、关节角度之类的机器人状态信息、剩余时间以及指令。然后它必须调用两个函数之一：give_up或move_eef。move_eef函数接收绝对位置、朝向，以及单臂或双臂的夹爪目标。接着一个非学习型的运动规划器会尝试执行，负责碰撞检测和关节路径规划。如果目标不可达或无效，模型会收到一条错误信息，可以重试。仿真环境RoboDojo是成功的唯一裁判。

segments.speaker: Noah
segments.en: Was the comparison on the leaderboard perfectly apples-to-apples?
segments.zh: 排行榜上的比较是完全公平的吗？

segments.speaker: John
segments.en: It's close, but not identical. The public policies were not rerun with the exact same wiki-derived task instructions that Astra received, so there's a minor difference in the input information. However, the more significant story is in the breakdown of Astra's performance. Its top rank isn't from being uniformly better. Looking at the results, Astra's average score was 28.97, compared to the second-place DM0.5 model's 24.90. But Astra was only strong on axes like 'Open' and 'Generalization'. On the 'Precision' axis, it scored a meager 4%, whereas DM0.5 scored over 16%.
segments.zh: 不完全一样，但很接近。公开的策略并没有用Astra收到的那套完全相同的、从wiki衍生出来的任务指令重新跑一遍，所以输入信息上有细微差别。不过更值得关注的是Astra表现的细分情况。它排名第一并不是因为全面占优。看结果，Astra的平均分是28.97，而第二名DM0.5模型是24.90。但Astra只在“开放性”和“泛化性”这些维度上表现强劲。在“精确性”维度上，它只拿到了可怜的4%，而DM0.5超过了16%。

segments.speaker: Noah
segments.en: So it's good at understanding open-ended instructions but poor at precise physical movements?
segments.zh: 所以它擅长理解开放式指令，但不太擅长精确的物理动作？

segments.speaker: John
segments.en: Exactly. A great example is the contrast between two tasks. On 'push_T', a task requiring semantic interpretation, Astra achieved 60% success where the next best policy got less than 1%. But on 'make_kong', which requires precise stacking, Astra scored 0% while another policy reached 90%. We see this anecdotally as well. In episodes requiring dynamic control, like picking an object off a moving conveyor belt, it would often miss. In another, it knocked over a tower while trying to place a block on top. Its strength is in semantic interpretation, not physical dexterity.
segments.zh: 没错。一个很好的例子就是两个任务之间的对比。在push_T这个需要语义理解的任务上，Astra达到了60%的成功率，而表现最好的其他策略还不到1%。但在make_kong这个需要精确堆叠的任务上，Astra的成功率是0%，而另一个策略达到了90%。我们在实际观察中也能看到类似的情况。在需要动态控制的任务中，比如从移动的传送带上抓取物体，它经常会抓空。还有一次，它在试图把积木放到塔顶时，反而把整座塔碰倒了。它的强项在于语义理解，而不是物理操作的灵巧性。

segments.speaker: John
segments.en: That naturally leads to the question of whether feedback or examples can fix this precision problem. The researchers tested this by providing one-shot demonstrations on a set of 34 tasks. The results were surprising. In the zero-shot baseline, the model succeeded on 78 out of 340 trials, for a 22.9% success rate. When given an image-based demonstration, the success rate fell to 17.9%. With a text-based demonstration, it fell further to 12.9%.
segments.zh: 这就自然引出一个问题：反馈或示例能不能解决这个精度问题？研究者在一组34个任务上做了单样本演示的测试。结果出人意料。在零样本基线下，模型在340次尝试中成功了78次，成功率22.9%。当给了一个基于图像的演示后，成功率降到了17.9%。而给了基于文本的演示后，更是降到了12.9%。

segments.speaker: Noah
segments.en: Hold on, demonstrations made it worse? That's the opposite of what you'd expect from in-context learning. Does this mean few-shot prompting is ineffective for robotics?
segments.zh: 等等，演示反而让效果更差了？这跟上下文学习的预期完全相反啊。那这是不是意味着少样本提示在机器人领域根本不管用？

segments.speaker: John
segments.en: The authors are careful not to make such a broad claim. This result is for one specific demonstration recipe, using examples from different layouts. Their hypothesis is that the model struggled to transfer the geometric specifics from the example to the new scene, or that the prompt interfered with its existing zero-shot precision. The performance decline mainly came from tasks Astra could already solve, suggesting the demonstrations added more noise than signal. They also ran a small probe with perturbations—mirroring the camera views or adding random jitter to movements. The model showed some ability to correct its actions, but the experiment couldn't isolate whether this was true adaptation or just standard closed-loop feedback.
segments.zh: 作者们很谨慎，没有下这么宽泛的结论。这个结果只针对一种特定的演示方案，用的是来自不同布局的示例。他们的假设是，模型难以把示例中的几何细节迁移到新场景，或者提示干扰了它原本的零样本精度。性能下降主要来自Astra本来就能解决的任务，说明这些演示带来的更多是噪声而非信号。他们还做了一个带扰动的小型探测实验——镜像相机视角，或者给动作加入随机抖动。模型表现出一定的动作纠正能力，但这个实验无法区分这到底是真正的自适应，还是只是标准的闭环反馈。

segments.speaker: John
segments.en: So to circle back to our opening question. This work shows that semantic reasoning and motor control don't have to be handled by separate systems. A single large model can, in some cases, reach directly into the control loop. However, its success is a sum of its parts: strong open-ended, semantic interpretation, and weak, unreliable physical execution. It is not a uniform replacement for specialized motor policies. The most sobering finding came from the real-world trials. The authors had to halt the official hardware evaluation because unsafe actions damaged the equipment, which firmly states that this approach has not yet established reliable or safe physical control.
segments.zh: 那么回到我们开头的问题。这项工作表明，语义推理和运动控制不一定非得由两套独立的系统来处理。单个大模型在某些情况下可以直接介入控制回路。但它的成功是各部分能力的总和：强大的开放式语义理解，加上薄弱且不可靠的物理执行。它并不能统一替代专门的运动策略。最令人清醒的发现来自真实世界的试验。作者不得不中止官方的硬件评估，因为不安全的行为损坏了设备，这明确说明该方法尚未建立起可靠或安全的物理控制。

segments.speaker: John
segments.en: Thanks for listening. If you have any further questions, ask our AI assistant or drop a comment.
segments.zh: 感谢收听。如果还有别的问题，可以问我们的AI助手，或者在评论区留言。
